newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's San Paolo hails deal with Dexia.
newsitem.headline: Italy's San Paolo hails deal with Dexia.

text.p: Italian banking group San Paolo's sale of 40 percent of its Crediop unit to Dexia signifies a step into one of the most important banking networks in Europe, Istituto Bancario San Paolo's chairman said.

Chairman Gianni Zandano said in a statement that with this move "Crediop and the whole San Paolo group enters into the most important European banking network specialising in financing local authorities and public works."
He said the deal with the Franco-Belgian banking group gave the Turin-based bank considerable possibilities of developing important synergies in Italian and international markets.
In the agreement announced earlier on Monday, Dexia also intends to buy a one percent stake in San Paolo bank when it is privatised from its controlling foundation.

"This new relationship of cooperation significantly broadens the network of San Paolo's international strategic alliances and is an important step in preparing the bank for the challenges of a single market and of European monetary union," Zandano said.
San Paolo said in lira terms the deal with Dexia would be worth between 480 to 565 billion lire ($290-$340 million).
